# Trace Element Analysis



## Checking for Diagenesis

### Maximum Threshold Concentration (MTC)

Source: Kamenov et al., 2018


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(gt)
library(dplyr)

Elements <- c("Mg", "Ca", "V", "Cr", "Mn", "Fe", "Ni", "Cu", "Zn", "Sr",
              "Ba", "La", "Ce", "Pr", "Nd", "Sm", "Eu","Gd" , "Tb", "Dy",
              "Ho", "Er", "Tm", "Yb", "Lu", "Pb", "Th", "U")

MTC <- c(6472, 462387, 0.11, 13.9, 15.4, 143, 46, 48, 629, 1700,
         40, 0.1, 0.12, 0.015, 0.058, 0.030, NA, NA, 0.002, 0.009,
         0.002, 0.008, 0.001, 0.021, 0.003, 63, 0.05, 0.05)

trace <- data.frame(Elements, MTC)
```
:::


### Normalizing your data (divide by the MTC)

1.  Transform data into a wide format


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Depending on the format of your data, transform the dataframe so that the rows represent the samples/individuals and the columns represent the trace elements.
```
:::


2.  Normalize each column by dividing by the MTC


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mtc <- trace$MTC[match(names(enamel)[-1], trace$Elements)] # ensures the elements are in the same order
mtc <- trace$MTC[match(names(enamel)[-1], trace$Elements)] 
# ensures the elements are in the same order
# if you have additional variables, exclude those as well in place of [-1] which removes the first column of sample names

mtc.ratio <- cbind(sample=enamel$sample, sweep(enamel[,-1], 2, mtc, "/")) 
# divides the sample values by the matched MTC values
# sweep(x, Margin, Stats, Fun)
```
:::


3.  Create a subset of Ratios


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyr)

elements <- c("V", "Mn", "Fe", "La", "Ce", "Nd", "Dy", "Yb", "Th", "U")

mtc.long <- mtc.ratio %>%
  select(sample, all_of(elements)) %>% 
  # pulls the sample numbers and the values for the subset of elements
  pivot_longer(-sample, names_to = "element", values_to = "ratio") 
  # transforms the table into a stacked format
```
:::


4.  Plotting the Normalized Concentrations


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mtc.long, aes(x=sample, y=ratio, group=element))+
  geom_point(aes(color=element))+
  geom_line(aes(color=element))+
  scale_y_log10() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10^0, color="red")+
  labs(x="Samples", y="C/MTC")
```

5.  Interpret the Data


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Dividing the sample concentrations by the maximum threshold concentrations obtained from modern individuals acts as a diagenesis check. If any value exceeds the 10^0 line, there is potential diagenic alteration to the sample.
```
